Solarpunk 1.3.0 hosting, rebuilt: players join with the game's own invite code, each server keeps its own Epic identity, and a world a player uploads keeps its owner's character.

## Server

### Added
- `SolarpunkServer.exe launch`: starts the game suspended, loads the given DLLs before the game's own code runs, then resumes it and prints `pid=<n>`. Options: `--exe`, `--workdir`, `--args` or `--args-file`, `--dll` (repeatable), `--optional-dll` (skipped when the file is missing), `--affinity <hex mask>`.
- `SolarpunkEosIdentity.dll` in `ue4ss-server`: keeps the server's Epic device sign-in in a file of its own instead of the Windows credential store, so every server on a machine gets its own Epic identity and peer-to-peer address. The file is `SP_EOS_IDENTITY_FILE` when set, else `ss_eos_identity.cred` in the game's `-UserDir`. Load it with `launch --optional-dll`; it must be in place before the game signs in to Epic, about 3 seconds after start.
- `"SeparateServerRecord": "on"` in the `Solarpunk` section of `appsettings.json` (with `"Transport": "eos"`): the first time a world is hosted, the hidden server player gets a saved record of its own, so the world owner's character in an uploaded single-player world stays the owner's. It runs once per world: a marker file next to the save stops a second copy, and a brand-new world just marks the server's own first record.

### Changed
- The host mod is the 0.1.92 line (no inventory stamp on invite-code servers) with the record and upload fixes, on the bundled mod loader with the string-lifetime fix (the 0.1.90 loader).
- Load the mod loader with `launch --dll` instead of injecting it after start. Loaded late, this loader can wait forever at "Verifying FName constructor".

### Fixed
- A world save uploaded with an older file time (FTP programs keep the original time) is now loaded instead of being set aside. The host keeps a record of the saves it wrote itself; an unknown `.sav` is a player's upload, and the previous world is kept in `_sundial_orphaned_saves`.

Players need nothing installed: in Solarpunk choose Multiplayer, Join session, Enter Code, and type the server's 5-letter code. The code changes each time the server starts.
